column4: dialect-gated per SUBTEST: a forEachDialect test, so mysql and mssql skip in these PostgreSQL-only jobs while postgres RUNS -- two, not three. Measured by NAME: CLEAT_TEST_POSTGRES=<pg> go test ./engine/ -run TestGetSecretRefusesAnotherTenantsRowOnEveryDialect -count=1 -json | grep '"Action":"skip"' reports exactly these two. The arms have to exist even where they skip: PostgreSQL and SQL Server enforce tenant scoping at the database (RLS and a SECURITY POLICY respectively), so a postgres-only run cannot vouch for the mssql arm's own enforcement mechanism, which is a different mechanism, not a copy.
